sidebar.title: Pilot onboarding
sidebar.subtitle: Six steps from an idea to a live ontology.

step1.title: Scope the pilot
step1.subtitle: A pilot is a narrow slice that proves the ontology in one domain before you scale out. Keep it focused — one process, one team, one or two weeks of data.
step1.scopePlaceholder: Which question will the pilot answer? Who needs the answer?
step1.scopeHint: One or two sentences. You can edit this later from the design workbench.

step2.title: Connect a source
step2.subtitle: Pick the data source the pilot reads from. The federation layer stays decoupled — you can register more sources later.
step2.connectionHint: Credentials are never stored in the browser — the final step registers them through the encrypted federation admin API.

step2b.title: Pick tables to introspect
step2b.subtitle: Select the subset the pilot needs, or run a full sweep. Selection is incremental — you can add more tables later from Design mode without redoing the analysis.

step3.title: Seed the glossary
step3.subtitle: Glossary terms are the business vocabulary. One per line, with the canonical term first and optional aliases separated by commas.
step3.draftPlaceholder:
Order — purchase, transaction
Customer — buyer
VIP tier — top-tier customer, loyalty
step3.draftHint: Drafted terms become CreateGlossaryTerm ops on Finish. You can refine them in the admin UI afterwards.

step4.title: Capture rules
step4.subtitle: Rules express invariants the LLM-generated queries must respect (SHACL). One per line in plain English — the design agent turns them into SHACL shapes later.
step4.draftPlaceholder:
Every Order has exactly one Customer
Order.status must be one of: placed, paid, fulfilled, cancelled
Amount is always non-negative
step4.draftHint: Ambiguous lines become clarification questions, not silent failures — the agent will ask.

step5.title: Map to topology
step5.subtitle: Tell us roughly how the source tables correspond to node types — one table per node is the common case; use the notes to describe exceptions.
step5.notesPlaceholder:
orders → Order
customers → Customer
order_items → bridge for Order←contains→Product
step5.notesHint: The design agent proposes ObjectMapping + LinkMapping entries from this plus the source schema.

step6.title: Validate and launch
step6.subtitle: You've captured the intent. Finish to hand over to the design agent — it materialises the ontology, runs introspection, and opens the workbench focused on your pilot.

small_sample.issue: Table '{table}' has only {row_count} rows. Sample statistics may not represent production data distribution.
small_sample.suggestion: Verify that enum values and ranges in this table are complete and representative.

opaque_enum_value.issue: Values [{sample_values}] include cryptic short code(s) [{short_cryptic}] whose meaning cannot be inferred from schema alone.
opaque_enum_value.suggestion: Provide the domain meaning for [{short_cryptic}] (e.g. 'N=24-hour specialty store'). It will be incorporated into the property description.

numeric_enum_code.issue: All observed values [{sample_values}] are integers with {distinct_count} distinct values — likely a numeric code whose semantics are unknown.
numeric_enum_code.suggestion: Provide the meaning for each code value, e.g. '1=active, 2=inactive, 3=suspended'.

sparse_property.issue: {null_pct}% of values are null ({null_count}/{row_count} rows). Property may be unused or conditionally populated.
sparse_property.suggestion: Confirm whether '{column}' is actively used or can be excluded from the ontology.

single_value_bias.issue: Only one value observed ('{observed_value}') across {row_count} rows. Production data may have additional values.
single_value_bias.suggestion: Confirm whether '{observed_value}' is the only possible value for '{column}', or provide the full expected set.

unmapped_source_table.issue: Source table '{table}' is not represented by any ontology node type.
unmapped_source_table.suggestion: Add a node type for '{table}' or explicitly exclude this table if it is intentionally out of scope.

unmapped_source_column.issue: Source column '{table}.{column}' has no corresponding property on node '{node_label}'.
unmapped_source_column.suggestion: Add a property for '{column}' on '{node_label}', or confirm it is intentionally excluded.

missing_foreign_key_edge.issue: Declared foreign key '{from_table}.{from_column} → {to_table}.{to_column}' is not represented by any ontology edge ({fk_count} relationship(s) but only {edge_count} edge(s) found).
missing_foreign_key_edge.suggestion: Add a distinct edge for '{from_table}.{from_column}' → '{to_table}', or confirm it should not become a graph relationship.

missing_containment_edge.issue: Inferred containment relationship '{from_table}.{from_column} → {to_table}.{to_column}' is not represented by any ontology edge ({fk_count} relationship(s) but only {edge_count} edge(s) found).
missing_containment_edge.suggestion: Add a distinct edge for '{from_table}.{from_column}' → '{to_table}', or confirm it should not become a graph relationship.

duplicate_edge.issue: {edge_count} edges between '{node_a}' and '{node_b}': [{edge_labels}]. Some may be semantically redundant.
duplicate_edge.suggestion: Review edges [{edge_labels}] between '{node_a}' and '{node_b}'. Remove duplicates that represent the same relationship.

node.issue: Node '{label}' has no description — the query translator lacks context for this entity type.
node.suggestion: Add a description for '{label}' explaining what this entity represents and its role in the domain.

node_property.issue: {label}.{property_name} has no description — the query translator cannot determine valid values or format.
node_property.suggestion: Provide a description for {label}.{property_name}: enum values, numeric range, or format hint.

edge.issue: [{label}] has no description — multi-hop traversal hints are missing.
edge.suggestion: Provide a description for [{label}] and add traversal hints for indirect queries.

edge_property.issue: [{label}].{property_name} has no description — the query translator cannot determine valid values or format.
edge_property.suggestion: Provide a description for [{label}].{property_name}: enum values, numeric range, or format hint.

orphan_node.issue: Node '{label}' has no incoming or outgoing edges — it is disconnected from the rest of the graph.
orphan_node.suggestion: Add edges connecting '{label}' to other node types, or remove it if it is not needed.

property_type_inconsistency.issue: Property '{property_name}' is defined with different types across node types: [{all_usages}].
property_type_inconsistency.suggestion: Verify that '{property_name}' should have different types, or unify to a single type for consistency.

hub_node.issue: Node '{label}' has {edge_count} edges (threshold: {threshold}). It may be a god-node that is doing too much.
hub_node.suggestion: Consider splitting '{label}' into more focused node types to reduce complexity.

overloaded_property.issue: Property '{property_name}' appears on {node_count} node types: [{node_labels}]. It may deserve its own node type or enum.
overloaded_property.suggestion: Consider extracting '{property_name}' into a dedicated node if the values represent a reusable domain concept.

self_referential_edge.issue: Edge [{label}] is self-referential: {node_label} → {node_label}. This creates a recursive/hierarchical relationship.
self_referential_edge.suggestion: Verify that [{label}] is intentional. Self-referential edges are valid for hierarchies (e.g. MANAGES, REPORTS_TO) but may also indicate a modelling error.
